question: Yash travels 200 km at 25 km/hr, the next 210 km at 21 km/hr and the next 204 km at 51 km/hr. What is his average speed (in km/hr) for the whole journey? (Round off your answer to two decimal places)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average speed is calculated as the ratio of total distance to total time.

Total Distance = 200 + 210 + 204 = 614 km

Total Time = (200 ÷ 25) + (210 ÷ 21) + (204 ÷ 51) = 8 + 10 + 4 = 22 hours

Average Speed = 614 ÷ 22 = 27.909... ≈ 27.91 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 27.91 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

D₁ = 200 km, S₁ = 25 km/hr

D₂ = 210 km, S₂ = 21 km/hr

D₃ = 204 km, S₃ = 51 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ T₁ = 200 ÷ 25 = 8 hours

⇒ T₂ = 210 ÷ 21 = 10 hours

⇒ T₃ = 204 ÷ 51 = 4 hours

⇒ Total Time = 8 + 10 + 4 = 22 hours

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 614 ÷ 22

⇒ Average Speed = 307 ÷ 11

⇒ Average Speed = 27.909... ≈ 27.91 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 27.91 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

If a person travels two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is directly given by (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If a person travels three equal distances at speeds x, y, and z, the average speed is directly given by (3 × x × y × z) ÷ (x×y + y×z + z×x).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the given speed by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.
